title: Heights & distances
examples: How do I find the height of a building if I know the angle?
What is the difference between elevation and depression angles?
Can I use this method if the angle is measured from the ground?

explain.say: Today we learn about angles of elevation and depression. These help us find heights and distances. Imagine looking up at the top of a tall object.
An angle of elevation is when you look up from your eye level. You measure the angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight. Think about climbing up a hill.
Next, we look at the angle of depression. This is when you look down from a higher point. For example, looking down from a window.
We use the tangent ratio for these problems. Tangent relates the opposite side to the adjacent side in a right triangle. Let us try a simple example together.

Suppose you measure an angle of elevation of thirty degrees. You stand ten meters away from a tree. You can find the height using tangent. The opposite side is the height, and the adjacent side is ten meters.

faq.q: What is the difference between elevation and depression?
faq.a: Elevation means looking up towards something higher than you. Depression means looking down from a higher point to something lower.
asks: What does looking down mean in trigonometry?

faq.q: Do I always use the tangent ratio?
faq.a: You use tangent when you know the distance along the ground and the angle. You use sine or cosine if you know the hypotenuse.
asks: When should I use sin instead of tan?
Is tangent always the right ratio for height problems?

faq.q: If the angle is of depression, do I still use the same math?
faq.a: Yes, because the angle of depression creates an alternate interior angle. This makes the angle inside the triangle equal to the angle of depression.
asks: Does depression angle change the calculation?
Can I just use the angle of depression directly?

faq.q: Do I need to know the height of my own eyes?
faq.a: Yes, sometimes the problem requires you to add your eye height to the calculated vertical height. Always check the wording carefully.
asks: Should I add my height to the answer?
Is my eye level important for these problems?

faq.q: What if the object is not straight up and down?
faq.a: If the object is slanted, you must first use trigonometry to find the vertical height component. You cannot assume it is perfectly vertical.
asks: What if the object is leaning?
How do I find the vertical height if it is angled?

facts: The angle of elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal line.
The angle of depression is measured downwards from the horizontal line.
In a right triangle, tangent equals opposite side divided by adjacent side.
The angle of depression angle equals the angle of elevation angle due to alternate interior angles.

quiz.say: A point on the ground makes an angle of elevation of forty-five degrees to the top of a pole. If the distance from the point to the pole is eight meters, what is the height?
quiz.why: Since the angle is forty-five degrees, the tangent value is one. Therefore, the height must equal the distance, which is eight meters.

wrong.0: This mistake occurs if the student mistakenly divides the distance by two, confusing the ratio.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the angle of elevation is given as forty-five degrees, which must be used in the calculation.
wrong.3: This mistake happens when students incorrectly multiply the distance by two, forgetting the trigonometric ratio.

quiz.say: From a cliff edge, an observer measures an angle of depression of twenty degrees to a boat. If the horizontal distance to the boat is fifty meters, what is the vertical drop?
quiz.why: The angle of depression creates an angle inside the triangle equal to twenty degrees. We use tangent to find the vertical drop, which is the opposite side.

wrong.0: This incorrectly rearranges the formula, treating the opposite and adjacent sides as swapped.
wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly suggests subtraction should be used instead of the tangent ratio.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the distance to the calculated height, treating them as separate measurements rather than related by the ratio.

quiz.say: A ladder leans against a wall. The angle the ladder makes with the ground is sixty degrees. If the base of the ladder is four meters from the wall, what is the height the ladder reaches on the wall?
quiz.why: The ladder, the wall, and the ground form a right triangle. We use the angle with the ground, which is sixty degrees, to find the opposite side (height).

wrong.1: This incorrectly swaps the roles of the opposite and adjacent sides in the tangent ratio.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly suggests adding the height and the base distance together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly subtracts the base distance from the calculated height.
